scope: Prospective computational feasibility pilot on newly generated synthetic internal coding contexts. Separate from the original independent biological-material protocol; no biological validation is claimed.
selection: Generate 24 length-90 internal standard-code contexts with seed 2689. Embed KLF at codons 11-13 (one based). Variable positions 33 and 39 are the K and F wobble sites. Require their pairing: exactly AU, GU, GC, forming a three-vertex path. Do not select by folding outcomes.
interventions: Odd/even contexts start with CUA/UUA Leu respectively. Targeted mutation changes that Leu first base C<->U, adjacent to the target hairpin closing pair. Matched control changes GGC<->GGU at codon 5. Both changes are one synonymous transition with identical GC change. Keep the peptide, three variable genotypes, target obligation, context length, temperature and all other bases fixed.
independence: No predictor is fitted to these ensemble outcomes. Generate contexts and commit predictions before running partition functions. Reject exact duplicates and >=80 percent identity over the complete 90nt against prior selected contexts and all 90nt windows in discovery contexts. Related variants are a single scaffold cluster. The shared motif is intentional; this is motif-specific model transfer, not independent biological replication or unrelated-family prediction.
prediction: Evaluate only the isolated one-pair five-base-loop hairpin energy against the unpaired state, using ViennaRNA eval_structure and RT at 310.15 K. Map energy to two-state occupancy 1/(1+exp(E/RT)). The exact path criterion predicts longest barrier L=max(0,min(score_AU,score_GC)-score_GU). Freeze baseline, targeted and control predictions before full ensemble pair probabilities. The two-state approximation omits competing conformations and uses the same energy parameters as validation.
endpoints: Full-ensemble target-pair marginal probabilities, longest all-threshold barrier lifetime L, integrated excess fragmentation I_E. Primary paired effect is (L_target-L_base)-(L_control-L_base). Report raw differences and all failures. Barrier classification uses L>=0.01. Intervention-direction accuracy requires a frozen predicted absolute change >=0.0001; observed absolute change <0.0001 counts as failure, not exclusion.
benchmarks: Compare isolated-hairpin predictions to all-connected (L=0) and generic Watson-Crick-over-GU barrier predictions; GC and mutation-count features predict no targeted-control difference by matching. Report errors, coverage and complete confusion counts. In-sample additive fits on three states are saturated and cannot discriminate any score field; demonstrate and report this limitation. Exact score permutations and 5 percent edge-roughness-conditioned permutations are descriptive references, not held-out predictors.
uncertainty: 10000 paired scaffold bootstrap resamples, seed 2689. This is variation across generated synthetic contexts, not experimental-replicate, biological, model-correctness or phylogenetic uncertainty. Conditional references are fully enumerated over six label permutations.
expansion_gate: At least 4 intervention predictions with absolute change >=0.0001; better lifetime MAE than L=0; direction accuracy >=0.75 on covered interventions; and a comparison that can distinguish the theory prediction from a saturated additive explanation. Report every gate, even if failed. Do not expand on a favorable subset. Failure means a bounded computational pilot, not evidence against biological RNA engineering.
not_established: folding-specific causality beyond the declared numerical model
